scenario.question: This is the deck's MODAL board: Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3) is our only creature, we have five untapped lands (four Mountain, Reliquary Tower) and our hand is NOT known. seat-3 (abaddon, 10 life) has Abaddon the Despoiler (5/5) untapped. seat-4 (sythis, 20 life) has Heliod, Sun-Crowned (5/5) and Setessan Champion (1/3) untapped plus Sphere of Safety. seat-2 has 40 life and no creature. (a) Using only the battlefield and its mana, can we deal any damage to any opponent this turn, and what stops us? (b) What is the minimum a card in hand must do for Zada's triggered ability to copy it across our board from THIS board state? Cite the rule for Zada's 'targets only' condition and for Sphere of Safety's attack cost.
notes: SUPERSEDED — this scenario was lifted by a bridge that silently omitted permanents, and both resolutions here reasoned from an incomplete board. Three defects, all found by the rules-checker reading THIS artifact and all fixed 2026-09-28: a creature with a characteristic-defining power (`Creature * / *`) never reached the board; an Aura was discarded as an instant; and a token was registered only when it ACTED, so the lift listed 10% of live tokens. Re-lifted as 011-sim-g59-t27-precombat-main. Kept because its resolver/checker exchange is what found the bugs — read it as history, never as a line.

WHY THIS BOARD. It is the deck's MODAL shape, not its best: across 100 seeded games at standard-v3 our seat had the commander out on 249 turns, and on 156 of them it had ONE other body or none. 79 turns were the commander completely alone. A ceiling proof on the widest board describes 2.0% of turns; this describes 63%.

HAND UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION, and here that IS the finding: with five mana and the commander in play, everything this deck can do depends on a card the log cannot show. That is precisely the judgment a goldfish channel cannot represent and a pilot can.
THE ACTIONS ARE AUTHORED. Both are offered so the resolver prices ATTACKING against HOLDING rather than assuming the attack; `observed_in_log: false` on both.

Our board is Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3, untapped) and five untapped lands: four Mountain and Reliquary Tower. scenario-facts confirms creature_bodies == [Zada, Hedron Grinder], other_permanents == [], spent_paying_a_cost == []. The hand is {unknown: 5} by construction, so part (a) is answered from battlefield resources only.
steps.effect: With priority in our own main phase and an empty stack we could cast anything in hand, but the log is an event stream and the hand is not reconstructed, so no card in hand may be assumed. Part (a) is therefore a question about five lands and one 3/3. scenario-facts card_membership: Zada, Hedron Grinder is in the deck; NOT_IN_THE_DECK is empty, so no card named in this scenario is outside the list. The board was lifted from a run of the zada-v1 BRANCH (slug goblin-storm@zada-v1), and Zada is the commander of both the branch and the sleeved 99, so the one card of ours on the battlefield is common to both.

steps.action: Enumerate the mana the battlefield can produce. Mountain: '{T}: Add {R}' (x4). Reliquary Tower: 'You have no maximum hand size. {T}: Add {C}'.
steps.effect: The maximum pool available this turn is {R}{R}{R}{R}{C} — five mana, of which at most four are red and one is colorless. Every one of these is a mana ability, so tapping these lands adds mana and does nothing else. The colorless mana from Reliquary Tower can pay a generic cost but can never pay a colored pip, which caps any line at four colored (red) pips.

steps.action: Enumerate every ability our battlefield offers that could deal damage. Zada, Hedron Grinder's oracle text is one triggered ability ('Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada, copy that spell for each other creature you control that the spell could target. Each copy targets a different one of those creatures.') and nothing else — no activated ability. The four Mountains and Reliquary Tower have only mana abilities. other_permanents is empty.
steps.effect: There is no damage-dealing spell or ability anywhere on our side of the battlefield. The five mana has no outlet: it can only be spent on something from a hand we are not allowed to assume. Consequently the ONLY route to damage this turn is combat damage, which an attacking creature deals equal to its power in the combat damage step. Our entire offense is 3 power.

steps.action: Test whether Zada can legally be declared as an attacker. She is untapped and is not a battle. The remaining requirement is haste or continuous control since the turn began.
steps.effect: Zada may attack PROVIDED she has been under our control continuously since this turn began. This is a stated assumption, not an observation: extras.reconstruction_notes says 'a creature's summoning sickness is not reconstructed (null)', and the scenario records summoning_sick: null for her. Supporting but not conclusive: the cut is turn 27, commander.zone is battlefield with casts == 1, and our graveyard already holds Broadside Bombardiers and two Goblin Token entries, so the board is not freshly assembled. If she in fact entered this turn, every attack line below is illegal and the answer to (a) becomes a flat no.

citations.quote: The chosen creatures must be untapped, they can’t also be battles, and each one must either have haste or have been controlled by the active player continuously since the turn began.
A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began.

steps.action: Price the cost of attacking at all, independent of which seat is attacked. Zada has no vigilance.
steps.effect: Declaring her as an attacker taps her. That is not a cost, but it is the consequence that matters on this board: our only creature — and the commander the whole deck is built on — is tapped for the remainder of the turn cycle and cannot block on any of the three opponents' turns. On the modal board this is the whole of our defense.

citations.quote: attacking simply causes creatures to become tapped

steps.action: Line A — declare Zada attacking seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 40 life). seat-2's board is exactly three lands: Undergrowth Stadium, Swamp, Overgrown Tomb. No creature, no enchantment, no attack tax.
steps.effect: No cost is required to attack this seat, and seat-2 cannot declare a blocker: the creatures chosen to block must be creatures the defending player controls, and seat-2 controls none. Zada is therefore unblocked and assigns combat damage equal to her power to seat-2: 3 damage, 40 -> 37. This is the one damage line on this board that no opposing choice can prevent. It is also nearly worthless: 3 into 40 is 7.5% of that seat's life, ~14 more identical turns to kill, against the pod's highest life total.

citations.quote: The defending player chooses which creatures they control, if any, will block. The chosen creatures must be untapped
Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power.

steps.action: Line B — declare Zada attacking seat-3 (abaddon, 10 life, the lowest in the pod). No attack tax exists on this seat. seat-3 controls Abaddon the Despoiler (5/5, untapped, no defender-side restriction), plus Talisman of Creativity, Fellwar Stone and five tapped lands.
steps.effect: The declaration is legal, but Abaddon the Despoiler is an untapped creature seat-3 controls and may be declared as a blocker. If it blocks: Zada is a blocked creature and assigns all 3 of her damage to Abaddon, which has toughness 5 and survives; seat-3 takes ZERO; and Abaddon's 5 damage to Zada is greater than her toughness of 3, so she is destroyed as a state-based action. We would lose the commander for no damage. Damage to seat-3 happens only if seat-3 declines to block, which is a choice belonging to the defending player and not a rules guarantee. Note it is the profitable line if unblocked: 10 -> 7.

A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it.
the total damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed

steps.action: Line C — declare Zada attacking seat-4 (sythis, 20 life). Sphere of Safety reads: 'Creatures can't attack you or planeswalkers you control unless their controller pays {X} for each of those creatures, where X is the number of enchantments you control.' Count the enchantments seat-4 controls from the board as lifted: Sphere of Safety (Enchantment) and Heliod, Sun-Crowned (Legendary Enchantment Creature — God). Sol Ring is an artifact, Setessan Champion is 'Creature — Human Warrior', and the six lands are lands.
steps.effect: X = 2, so Sphere of Safety is an attack restriction of the form 'can't attack unless some condition is met', and a declaration of Zada as an attacker against seat-4 is ILLEGAL unless we pay {2} for her. Because Zada requires paying a cost to attack, the total cost to attack is determined and locked in during the declare attackers step. We can pay it: {2} from two Mountains (or a Mountain plus Reliquary Tower's {C}, since generic costs take any type of mana), leaving 3 mana. Heliod counts toward X whether or not it is currently a creature — it is an enchantment either way — so X = 2 is robust to the devotion question raised in step 9.

If any of the chosen creatures require paying costs to attack, or if any optional costs to attack were chosen, the active player determines the total cost to attack.

steps.action: Having paid, test what seat-4 can block with. Setessan Champion is recorded as 1/3 and untapped. Heliod, Sun-Crowned is recorded as 5/5 and untapped, but its oracle text reads 'As long as your devotion to white is less than five, Heliod isn't a creature.'
steps.effect: Setessan Champion alone is enough: it is an untapped creature seat-4 controls, it may block Zada, and a block reduces damage to seat-4 to zero (the Champion dies to 3 damage against toughness 3; Zada, taking 1, lives). So {2} buys an attack that the defender can blank for free. A FINDING on the lifted board, offered as an observation rather than a load-bearing step: counting white pips among seat-4's recorded permanents gives Heliod {2}{W} = 1 and Sphere of Safety {4}{W} = 1, a devotion to white of 2, which is less than five — on the board exactly as reconstructed Heliod is NOT a creature and could not be declared as a blocker at all, despite the scenario recording a 5/5 (its printed power and toughness). The bridge does not reconstruct devotion, and extras.reconstruction_notes already warns that creature state is partially unobserved, so an unrecorded white permanent or Aura could change this. It does not change the conclusion, because the Champion can block regardless.

steps.action: Answer (a) from steps 2-9: can we deal any damage to any opponent this turn using only the battlefield and its mana, and what stops us?
steps.effect: YES, but only 3 damage, and only one seat cannot refuse it. Best case by seat: seat-2 3 damage GUARANTEED (no blockers exist) taking 40 -> 37; seat-3 3 damage ONLY IF they decline to block with an untapped 5/5, and blocking costs us the commander; seat-4 3 damage only after paying {2} and only if they decline to block with an untapped body. The pod total available this turn is 3 damage to ONE seat — not 3 per seat and not 9 across the pod. What stops us, precisely: (1) one body, so 3 power is the ceiling on all combat damage; (2) no damage-dealing ability anywhere on our battlefield, so five mana is stranded with no outlet and cannot convert into a single point of damage; (3) Sphere of Safety taxes any attack on the 20-life seat by {2} per creature; (4) both low-life seats (10 and 20) hold untapped creatures that can blank the attack for free, while the only defenseless seat is the one at 40; (5) attacking taps our only creature and commander, which is also our only blocker. The refutation is the result: there is no line on this battlefield that deals meaningful damage, and the modal board is why.

steps.action: Begin (b). State the trigger condition of Zada's ability exactly: 'Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada, copy that spell for each other creature you control that the spell could target.' Identify the three conditions a card in hand must satisfy for the ability to trigger at all.
steps.effect: The ability triggers only when a game event matches its trigger event, so all three must hold: (i) the card must be an INSTANT or SORCERY — a creature, artifact, enchantment, land or planeswalker card cannot trigger it, and neither can an activated ability; (ii) we must CAST it — a copy put onto the stack by another effect is not cast and does not re-trigger; (iii) every target it has must be Zada and nothing else — targets are declared as the spell is put on the stack, so a spell that also targets another creature, a player, or a permanent we do not control simply never triggers the ability. Wizards' own ruling agrees on (iii) and on the copies not being cast, but the CR is the citation here.

citations.quote: Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers.
These targets are declared as part of the process of putting the spell or ability on the stack.

steps.action: Resolve the copy count FROM THIS BOARD STATE. Zada's ability copies the spell 'for each other creature you control that the spell could target'. Enumerate the set: creatures we control = {Zada, Hedron Grinder} (scenario-facts creature_bodies, one entry; other_permanents empty; no tokens on the battlefield — the two Goblin Token entries are in the graveyard, and extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions records 2 unobserved token resolutions for our seat, which the bridge did NOT place on the battlefield). Creatures we control OTHER than Zada = {} — the empty set.
steps.effect: The set the copy clause iterates over is empty, so the triggered ability triggers, goes on the stack, resolves, and creates ZERO copies. A copy is only created for an object that is a legal target, and only permanents are legal targets for such a spell — there is no second permanent creature for a copy to target, so no copy exists to be put onto the stack. This is the crux: on the deck's MODAL board, a perfectly-chosen Zada spell is an ordinary one-target spell. Paying four mana for 'targets only Zada' buys exactly one instance of the effect, on a 3/3 — the engine is switched on and multiplies by one.

citations.quote: a copy isn’t created for that player or object
Only permanents are legal targets for spells and abilities

steps.action: Test whether ONE card in hand could bootstrap the copy itself — e.g. an instant or sorcery that targets only Zada and also creates a creature token as it resolves.
steps.effect: It cannot. Zada's triggered ability is put on the stack after the spell is cast and becomes the TOPMOST object, above the spell that triggered it; the top object resolves first. So the triggered ability resolves — and counts our other creatures — strictly BEFORE the spell that triggered it resolves. Any body that the spell itself would create arrives too late to be copied for. The same ordering is what the official ruling describes when it says the original spell sits beneath the copies and resolves last. Therefore no single instant or sorcery in hand can produce even one copy from this board.

citations.quote: The ability becomes the topmost object on the stack.
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

steps.action: State the answer to (b): the MINIMUM a card in hand must do, as required properties rather than a named card (the hand is unknown by construction and may not be assumed).
steps.effect: From THIS board state the minimum is a TWO-CARD sequence, because one card cannot satisfy both halves. Half one — a card that puts at least one creature other than Zada onto our battlefield and does so BEFORE the Zada spell is cast: any creature spell, or any permanent/token-maker that resolves first. Half two — an instant or sorcery we cast whose EVERY target is Zada and nothing else. Two further properties are load-bearing on the new body: it must be on the battlefield as a creature we control when the triggered ability resolves, and it must be a legal target for every instance of the word 'target' on that spell — so a spell reading 'target creature you control' works, while one reading 'target Goblin you control' requires the body to be a Goblin, and a body with shroud or the wrong protection is skipped and yields no copy. Mana is the binding constraint on the pair: the combined cost must fit {R}{R}{R}{R}{C}, i.e. at most four colored pips, all of them red, with Reliquary Tower's colorless mana usable only for generic. Yield: each additional other creature adds exactly one copy, so the first body takes the multiplier from 1 to 2.

citations.quote: The copies are put onto the stack with those targets in the order of their controller’s choice.
Colored mana in costs can be paid only with the appropriate color of mana.

final_state.summary: (a) YES but trivially: the battlefield can deal at most 3 damage, to exactly one seat. Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3) is our only creature and no permanent we control has a damage-dealing ability, so combat is the only route and 3 power is the ceiling; the five untapped lands ({R}{R}{R}{R}{C}) have no outlet and are stranded. Only seat-2 cannot refuse the damage — it controls three lands and no creature, so Zada is unblockable there for 3 (40 -> 37), the worst seat to hit. seat-3 (10 life) keeps Abaddon the Despoiler 5/5 untapped: a block deals seat-3 zero and DESTROYS our commander. seat-4 (20 life) costs {2} to attack under Sphere of Safety (X = 2 enchantments: Sphere of Safety + Heliod) and still has an untapped blocker. Attacking also taps our only creature and only blocker. (b) From this board Zada's ability copies NOTHING: the clause iterates over 'each other creature you control', and that set is empty, so a perfectly-chosen spell that targets only Zada resolves as an ordinary single-target spell. No single card in hand can fix this — the triggered ability is the topmost object on the stack and resolves before the spell that triggered it, so a token the spell itself makes arrives too late. The minimum is a two-card sequence: one card that puts at least one other creature we control onto the battlefield first, plus an instant or sorcery we cast whose every target is Zada, with the new body a legal target for every instance of 'target' on that spell — the combined cost fitting four red pips plus one colorless. The first extra body takes the multiplier from 1 to 2.

disagreements_with_prose: The authored actions offer only 'attack seat-3' and 'declare no attackers'. A third line exists and is better on damage: seat-2 controls no creature, so an attack there deals 3 that no choice can prevent. The note's reasoning ('seat-2 is at 40 with no creature to race') is about VALUE, not legality, and is correct on value — but the question asked whether ANY damage is possible, and against seat-2 it is.
